models.name: todo_list_system_config
models.description: System-wide configuration and metadata storage for the Todo List application. This table maintains operational settings, feature flags, and deployment-specific configuration that applies across the entire system. Configuration entries are stored as key-value pairs with type information and versioning, enabling flexible management of system behavior without database schema migrations.

plainFields.name: config_key
plainFields.description: Unique configuration key identifier. Examples: 'max_todos_per_user', 'enable_feature_flag_xyz', 'deployment_environment', 'token_expiration_minutes'. Used to lookup specific configuration values.

plainFields.name: config_value
plainFields.description: Configuration value as string. The actual value is stored as string for flexibility; type conversion handled by application based on value_type field. Examples: '10000', 'true', 'production', '900'.

plainFields.name: value_type
plainFields.description: Data type of the configuration value. Valid values: 'string', 'integer', 'boolean', 'float'. Used by application to parse and convert config_value to appropriate type for processing.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description explaining the purpose and usage of this configuration setting. Helps operations team understand what this setting controls and when it should be modified.

plainFields.name: version
plainFields.description: Version number of this configuration entry. Incremented each time the value is updated. Starts at 1 for new entries. Enables tracking of configuration evolution over time.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration entry was initially created in UTC. Immutable after creation. Used for audit trail and history tracking.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration entry was last modified in UTC. Updated whenever the config_value or other fields change. Used to track most recent configuration updates.

models.name: todo_list_users
models.description:
User accounts and authentication credentials for the Todo List application.

Stores registered user information including email address, securely hashed password, and account metadata. Each user has a one-to-many relationship with sessions (supporting multi-device login) and password reset tokens. Users are the core identity entity that owns all todo items and authentication sessions.

User accounts are created during registration with email validation and unique email constraint. Passwords are hashed using bcrypt (never stored plaintext). Account status is tracked implicitly through the deleted_at field - null means active account, non-null timestamp indicates deleted account.

This table is fundamental to all authentication and authorization in the system. Every authenticated operation references a user ID from this table.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: User's email address used for login and account recovery. Must be unique across all users to prevent duplicate accounts. Stored in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Secure bcrypt hash of user's password (minimum cost factor 10). Never stored or returned as plaintext. Used for password verification during login using secure comparison functions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when user account was created (immutable). Recorded in UTC timezone, ISO 8601 format.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent account modification. Updated when password changes or account information is modified. Recorded in UTC timezone.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when account was deleted (soft delete marker for audit trail). Null value indicates active account. When set to non-null, user cannot log in and associated sessions/tokens should be invalidated.

plainFields.name: last_login_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of user's most recent successful login. Updated each time user authenticates. Used for tracking user activity and session management.

models.name: todo_list_sessions
models.description:
User authentication sessions for managing multi-device login support.

Represents an authenticated session from a specific device or browser. Each user can have multiple concurrent sessions from different devices, and this table tracks each independent session separately. Sessions store device context (IP address, user agent) and token associations for revocation tracking.

Sessions are created upon successful login and contain references to both the user and the generated JWT tokens (if using database-backed token storage). Sessions are invalidated on logout or when tokens expire.

This table enables the multi-device login requirement where a user can be logged in from multiple devices simultaneously, with independent token management per device. Each session maintains its own expiration and can be revoked independently.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the user who owns this session. {@link todo_list_users.id}

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address from which the session was established. Used for session context tracking and security monitoring to detect unusual login patterns.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: HTTP User-Agent header from the device that established the session. Contains information about browser/device type. Used to display device information to users and detect suspicious sessions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when session was created (login time). Recorded in UTC timezone, ISO 8601 format. Used for tracking session duration and age.

plainFields.name: last_activity_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent API request using this session. Updated on each authenticated request. Used for implementing inactivity timeout (7 days) and session activity tracking.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when session was explicitly terminated (logout). Null while session is active. When set, all tokens associated with this session become invalid and cannot be reused.

plainFields.name: absolute_timeout_at
plainFields.description: Absolute maximum expiration time for this session (30 days from creation). Session must be terminated by this time regardless of activity. Used for enforcing maximum session duration per security requirements.

models.name: todo_list_password_reset_tokens
models.description:
Secure tokens for password reset functionality enabling account recovery.

Generated when users forget their password and request recovery. Each token is time-limited (1 hour validity) and single-use to prevent token reuse attacks. Tokens are cryptographically secure random values that cannot be guessed or brute-forced.

When user clicks password reset link in email, the token is validated (not expired, not already used), then user can set new password. After password reset completes, the token is marked as used (consumed) to prevent reuse.

This table implements the secure password recovery flow required by the authentication system. Tokens are tied to specific users and are invalidated upon successful password change.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the user who requested password reset. {@link todo_list_users.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Cryptographically secure random token value used in password reset link. Must be unique and unguessable. Sent to user via email in reset link (e.g., /reset-password?token={token}). Hashed before storage for security.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when reset token was generated. Used to calculate expiration time (tokens valid for 1 hour). Recorded in UTC timezone.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this reset token becomes invalid. Set to 1 hour from creation. Tokens cannot be used after this time and user must request new reset link.

plainFields.name: consumed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when token was successfully used to reset password. Null while token is unused. When set, token can no longer be used (prevents reuse attacks). Single-use enforcement.

models.name: todo_list_token_blacklist
models.description:
Revoked JWT tokens to prevent reuse after logout or password change.

When a user logs out or changes their password, their JWT tokens must be invalidated to prevent unauthorized access if tokens were compromised. This table maintains a blacklist of revoked token identifiers (JTI - JWT ID claim) so the system can reject attempts to use invalidated tokens.

Each revoked token entry includes the unique token identifier (jti from token payload), user who owned the token, and revocation timestamp. The table also stores token expiration time so entries can be automatically cleaned up after tokens naturally expire (no need to maintain blacklist entries forever).

This enables secure token revocation without requiring a database lookup on every request (tokens can validate their JTI against blacklist on presentation). Implements the security requirement that tokens cannot be reused after logout or password change.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the user who owned the revoked token. {@link todo_list_users.id}

plainFields.name: token_jti
plainFields.description: Unique token identifier from JWT payload (jti claim). Used to identify which specific token was revoked. Combined with user_id to prevent token reuse by same user.

plainFields.name: revoked_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when token was revoked (logout or password change). Used for audit trail of when revocation occurred.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the original JWT token was set to expire. Blacklist entries can be automatically cleaned up after this time since token would be expired anyway. Enables automatic garbage collection of old revocation records.

plainFields.name: revocation_reason
plainFields.description: Reason why token was revoked: 'logout' (user initiated logout), 'password_change' (user changed password and all sessions revoked), or 'global_logout' (user logged out from all devices). Useful for security auditing.

models.name: todo_list_todos
models.description:
Personal todo items managed by authenticated users.

Stores individual todo tasks created by users, each with exclusive user ownership enforced through user_id foreign key. Enables complete data isolation - each user can only view, edit, and delete their own todos. Supports core todo management functionality: creation with title and optional details, completion status tracking, metadata (due date, priority), and modification history through timestamps.

Designed for minimal viable todo application scope focusing on essential CRUD operations, filtering by completion status, and sorting capabilities. Single unified list per user with no categories, projects, or advanced organizational features in baseline implementation.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Owner of this todo. References authenticated user who created this todo. {@link todo_list_users.id}

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Todo task title. Required field, non-empty after trimming whitespace. What the todo is about. Length 1-255 characters.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional detailed description of the todo task. Additional context or notes. Length 0-5000 characters. Null or empty when not provided.

plainFields.name: completed
plainFields.description: Completion status of the todo. True = completed and done, false = pending/incomplete. Initialized to false when created. Can be toggled by user at any time.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: Optional due date for completing this todo. Must be today or in the future (cannot be in past). In ISO 8601 format. Null when not set.

plainFields.name: priority
plainFields.description: Priority level for this todo. One of: "low", "medium", "high". Defaults to "medium" if not specified. Optional field.

plainFields.name: completed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when todo was marked as complete. Recorded when completion status changes to true. Cleared when marked incomplete. Null while todo is pending.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when todo was created. System-generated, immutable. Used for sorting (newest/oldest first) and audit purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when todo was last modified. Updated whenever any field changes (title, description, completion status, priority, due date). Tracks modification history.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Marked when todo is deleted by user. Null for active todos. Enables potential recovery and audit trail of deletions.
